Review scope

Draft for owner review. Structure matters; style is provisional. This is the Stitch-based UI documentation pilot and gameplay extension, not an approved final interface or a working Android app. Confirmed branding: Async Tabletop Wizards; subtitle: Specialized tabletop simulator for asynchronous wizardry (D-292).

Review editions: PDF download · Markdown source.

Cumulative owner direction: feedback and explicit supersessions. Later rounds retain earlier decisions unless the owner explicitly changes them. This full document is republished at the same browser-refresh URL after changes. The D-292 fullscreen/navigation/copy revisions below are confirmed direction; remaining geometry/style proposals are not silently approved by this round.

Both portrait and landscape are required (D-290). Each screen below has a 412 × 892 portrait capture and an 892 × 412 landscape capture. These are logical pixel/dp-like design viewports, not physical screen pixels or a promise about every Android device. The landscape image is a real rendering of the responsive design at the short, wide viewport—not a rotated or stretched portrait image.

The packet covers account entry, navigation, games/invitations, contacts, saved decks, import and lobby preparation, plus the D-291 gameplay extension: live table, fixed Hand, central Stack/combat, paused/running history, armed historical continuation and the explicit Redo route. G00 and U01 retain the original pilot’s empty board for provenance, not as the current gameplay design. Reveal trays, full card/zone menus, inspectors, chat and ending overlays still need their own visual state completion; their behavior is not removed.

Reading the mockups

  • Text button: a labeled action such as “Ready” or “Accept.” A leading icon does not turn it into an unlabeled icon button.
  • Icon button: Back arrow or password-visibility eye. The proposed normal target is at least 48 × 48 logical pixels, with an accessible name.
  • Label/status: descriptive text such as “Ready,” “Invitation pending,” or a card count. A checkmark complements text rather than replacing it with color.
  • Field: an explicitly labeled text input, search input or multiline pasted list. Password contents are not silently trimmed or normalized.
  • Thumbnail: an abstract placeholder with a card-name fallback. No production card artwork was requested for this pilot.
  • Muted action: unavailable, with a visible reason. It is not a future feature hidden behind a paywall or an instruction to bypass a failed requirement.
  • Scroll: long lists and forms scroll within their content panel. Main actions must remain reachable in both orientations; an initial viewport is not the entire possible list. On-screen keyboard, large-text and split-screen variants still need their own later visual checks.

Fullscreen (D-292): no system status/navigation strip or dedicated app-title bar. Necessary hamburger, Back, phase/history and other actions remain compact in-screen controls, not branding chrome. Ordinary labels, game-state feedback and errors are not forbidden “status bars.” Review targets remain roughly 16 px outer margins, 12 px gaps and 48 px controls, without reserving fake system-bar space. Native cutouts, temporary OS bar reveal, keyboard and accessibility still need safe placement/verification; these are not implemented Android claims.

Important: these are static mockups. Their behavior is specified in the notes, not demonstrated by functioning buttons. An incidental label/decoration in a generated image does not authorize a feature that contradicts those notes.

Navigation overview

Sign in ↔ Create account
   └─ Forgot password → email link → New password → Sign in
Hamburger navigation (persistent on landscape non-gameplay screens)
   ├─ Menu → main menu (Games / Manage decks / Contacts)
   │   ├─ Manage decks → deck details → rename / cover / re-import / delete
   │   │              └─ Import → resolve all entries → save new or replace
   │   └─ Contacts → username search → Add contact → Invite
   ├─ Games → games browser (Games first, Invitations afterward)
   │   └─ each current game → its table or lobby, according to lifecycle state
   │       ├─ In play → G01 live table ↔ H01/H02 history
   │       └─ Setup → choose/prepare deck → Ready
   └─ Logout (fixed footer outside scroll area) → signed-out entry
Games browser → Accept invitation → same lobby
              └─ New game → Contacts → Invite → waiting lobby
Lobby → both Ready → G01 live table
History → Continue playing from here → H03 armed intent
    ├─ Cancel / Return to live → no shared change
    └─ first successful mutation → active continuation

Back leaves a screen; it is not a game cancellation, Ready withdrawal, gameplay Undo or publication step. Rotation preserves the current screen and surviving in-process input/selection; it does not repeat a request or submit an unfinished form. Saved decks, contacts and games synchronize across devices, but unfinished forms and personal navigation are not automatically cross-device shared state.

Layout choices being proposed

The following remain UI proposals, not new behavior approvals: Contacts’ “Invite” placement, list/grid arrangements outside the confirmed D-292 navigation, authentication forms other than A01’s selected same-card composition, two-column landscape panels, import review/save routing, cover-selection confirmation, destructive-action dialogs and the read-only reconnect escape. “Random” is selected in the example lobby state; these images do not choose a universal initial starter default or retention policy.

For gameplay, the owner selects a trial own Hand hovering above the fixed bottom controls, central Stack/combat lanes, hold Undo for Redo and pause-on-drag history. Green bands and orientation-specific left/middle special-zone controls follow the owner’s layout brief. Opponent top Hand, life placement, phase/mode shapes, camera geometry and colors remain proposals. See G01–G03 and H01–H03; agreement to try a layout is not approval of final sizes or a passed UI gate.

Existing rules are applied without asking for approval again: no guest/social login, contact approval, full saved-deck builder, score archive, host Start, extra Send, online-presence requirement, automatic opening draw, in-game Sideboard or in-app notification mute controls.

The primary repository source is docs/design/03-contracts/accounts-decks-and-lobby.md. The Android experience contract and technical notification profile add platform/recovery constraints. Gameplay additionally follows board-and-controls.md, history-and-undo.md, history-grouping.md, combat-stack-and-projections.md and the clarified ../gameplay-screen-proposal.md. These are source anchors, not extra required reading to understand the packet’s interaction notes. These source references are repository documents, not extra pages required to read the hosted packet. Decision references below identify already agreed behavior; the particular control geometry remains proposed.

Suggested review

Refer to a screen ID and orientation, for example “L04 landscape: make the sideboard narrower.” Review the hierarchy, approximate space allocation, icon-versus-text choices, visibility of actions and the state transitions. Colors, fonts and borders remain provisional; the app name/subtitle are confirmed.

A01 — Sign in

Layout (confirmed D-292): both orientations center the same bounded login card, including app name/subtitle, without a landscape intro/form split. The short landscape viewport scrolls this unchanged card rather than shrinking targets or switching composition. Email and Password are text fields; the eye is an icon button. Sign in, Create account and Forgot password are labeled actions. The image deliberately includes an example credential error; a clean initial form omits that message.

Interaction: Sign in submits credentials. Failure keeps inputs available for correction; success opens the main menu or resumes the same-account return context. A valid existing login skips this screen across ordinary restarts and inactivity. No guest entry, alternate social provider or routine session expiry. Password visibility is personal UI only. Back does not sign another device out.

Basis: D-188, D-197, D-217, D-249, D-268, D-289, D-292.

A02 — Create account

Layout: Username, Email and Password are fields. The password eye is an icon; Create account and Sign in are text actions. Landscape uses the width for an intro/form split and allows the form panel to scroll, not smaller touch targets.

Interaction: registration uses these three credentials; username is public player identity while email is private. Invalid input/network failure stays on this form with a specific inline explanation and preserved editable input. The proposed successful route returns to A01 with a success notice and known email populated; it does not invent an email-verification gate. No confirmation password, social login or profile editor is required by this draft. Password whitespace/Unicode handling stays consistent with sign-in and reset.

Basis: D-197, D-249; success navigation and exact feedback are UI proposals.

A02b — Registration: lower form

Same screen, different scroll position: the short landscape form panel is scrolled to its bottom to expose Create account and the Sign in link at full touch size. The portrait form fits already, so that capture is unchanged. This is not a separate registration step, new server state or submission. It makes the landscape scrolling cost visible rather than hiding it in the tap budget.

A03 — Password reset email

Layout: one Email field, Send reset link text button, neutral submitted-state notice and Back to sign in. The initial state uses the same structure without the submitted notice. No session/sign-in explanation on the screen (D-292). The sample email is synthetic, not account data.

Interaction: request an email reset link without revealing whether that address is registered. A delivery/request failure keeps the address editable and shows a retryable inline error; it does not claim the password changed. Merely requesting or opening a reset link does not revoke sessions. The successful email-link flow continues at A04, not an invented six-digit-code screen.

Basis: D-197, D-279; neutral response follows the authentication profile.

A04 — Set a new password

Layout: New password is a field; its eye is an icon button. Change password is a text button. The valid reset-link state is shown. Email and username are not additional editable account settings here. Remove session/sign-in explanations and generic reassurance copy from the screen (D-292); the behavior below remains. The compact form is centered without an empty landscape explanation panel.

Interaction: successful reset changes the password and revokes existing sessions for new requests, then returns to Sign in with a success notice. An expired/invalid/already-used link instead shows a non-actionable error and a Request another link route to A03; it does not submit a reset or revoke sessions. Do not silently trim password contents. Already-authorized/in-flight requests may still finish normally; the UI must not promise recall of those operations.

Basis: D-197, D-249, D-279, D-289. Alternate link/error state is described here but not separately pictured in this pilot.

N01 — Main menu

Layout (D-292): Games, Manage decks and Contacts are large icon-plus-text destinations, without explanatory subtitles/marketing text. No notification-settings or direct Logout link in main-menu content. Landscape includes the shared persistent navigation; portrait uses the hamburger. See N02 for its open state.

Interaction: Games opens P01; Manage decks opens D01; Contacts opens P02. Logout from the navigation footer immediately clears this device’s login and private downloads, returning to A01 without deleting server games/decks or logging out independent devices. Remote revocation is best effort. This proposed layout does not add a routine logout confirmation or expose account-email data in shared player lists.

Basis: D-188, D-196, D-218, D-220, D-241, D-282, D-289, D-292.

N02 — Shared Menu / Games navigation

Confirmed structure (D-292): Menu and Games are clickable top-level destinations, not expand-only headers. Menu opens N01; its indented subitems are Manage decks and Contacts only. Games opens P01; its indented list contains each current game, including waiting/preparation states, not a separate Lobbies category. Task screens needing a selected deck/game stay in their contextual routes.

Scrolling: the category/subitem/game area scrolls independently; Logout stays in a fixed non-scrolling bottom footer. Portrait hamburger opens this drawer; Close, Back or tapping outside dismisses it without a shared change. Landscape non-gameplay screens always show the navigation alongside content. Gameplay in either orientation keeps it collapsed until the hamburger is used; it must not permanently reduce the landscape board. A modal temporarily blocks background navigation until dismissed. Rotation retains the current destination and unfinished input while switching navigation presentation, not issuing another request.

State: game rows open that same game’s current table or lobby. Setup → play, return-to-lobby, acceptance and cancellation update the same listing under existing server lifecycle rules; no duplicated “lobby versus game” identity. Incoming invites not yet accepted remain in P01’s Invitations section, not playable own-game rows. Example usernames/status labels are synthetic; row geometry remains reviewable.

Provenance: locally composed inert design derivative, not a new Stitch screen or working navigation. The surrounding screenshots apply the same shared shell.

P01 — Games and invitations

Layout (D-292): one Games list contains in-play and setup/lobby states; Invitations follows it, not before or as a separate left-hand first column. Accept/Decline, Open, Reinvite and New game are text actions; necessary lifecycle status labels distinguish rows without inventing a structural Lobbies category. The same order applies in landscape, beside persistent navigation; lists scroll.

Interaction: Accept enters the exact existing lobby as L02, without Ready or an immediate start. Decline retains the inviter’s lobby/preparation/Ready. Reinvite addresses that lobby, not a replacement game. Invitations do not expire automatically; cancelling a game removes its invitation and current listing. Open active game reaches G01; a setup row opens its existing lobby. New game opens P02. An empty list would show “No current games” with New game, not a finished-game archive.

Basis: D-188, D-195, D-208, D-209, D-214, D-287, D-292. Empty/loading states are not separate mockups yet; no unread/read, presence or result statistics are implied.

P02 — Contacts and new game

Layout: Search usernames is a field; search magnifier is a supporting icon. Search, Add contact and Invite are labeled text actions. Saved contacts and search results remain separate. No email addresses or online-status dots.

Interaction: Search produces explicit username matches; Add contact saves a contact directly with no friend-request approval. A newly saved contact gets Invite in the contact list. Invite creates a game plus its first invitation and opens L01. There is no extra confirmation/selection wizard or automatic recipient acceptance. No results uses an inline “No matching usernames” notice, not a missing-user substitution. Removing contacts is not invented by this pilot.

Basis: D-195, D-196, D-197, D-218. Exact search matching is not settled by these example names or the placement of the Search button.

D01 — Saved decks

Layout: named deck rows/cards use cover placeholders and descriptive mainboard/sideboard counts. Import deck is a labeled text action with a supporting icon. Opening a deck goes to D02. An empty collection keeps Import deck visible.

Interaction: collection names/lists/covers synchronize between the account’s devices. Saved card-list changes happen through import, not individual quantity editors or a deck-builder search. No Export, legality badge, restore bin, win-rate statistics or gameplay Undo for collection deletion. Missing artwork uses the deck/card text fallback and does not prevent import or deck selection.

Basis: D-189, D-198, D-199, D-218, D-221, D-241, D-271.

D02 — Saved deck details

Layout: Name/Rename and cover/Choose cover are metadata controls. Re-import and Delete saved deck are text actions. Mainboard/Sideboard tabs only choose which read-only saved list is displayed; they are not in-game zone controls. Landscape puts metadata beside that list.

Interaction: proposed Rename opens a small name-field dialog with Save name and Cancel; it cannot change card quantities. Choose cover opens D05. Re-import opens D03 with this saved deck as a replacement candidate. Delete opens D06. Saving or deleting this collection entry never rewrites copies already selected in a lobby/game. Card names and counts in the mockup are illustrative synthetic data, not a real valid import or a required deck-size rule.

Basis: D-189, D-199, D-221. Rename’s edit state is described but not separately pictured; naming/duplicate policies are not inferred from the example.

D03 — Import with unresolved names

Layout: Deck list is a multiline text field, not a card builder. The error identifies the unresolved line. Review import is unavailable while entries are unresolved. Landscape uses an input/issues split; input and feedback must both remain reachable rather than squeezing the text area into a one-line field.

Interaction: accept ordinary quantity/name lists, common optional printing suffixes and supported mainboard/sideboard separators. Correct the pasted text or retry lookup; never silently choose an ambiguous card or save a partial list. Nothing replaces a saved deck on lookup/transport failure. When all entries resolve, Review import advances to D04. Art downloading and obtaining the newest entire catalog are not save prerequisites. No separate Send/definition-upload UI.

Basis: D-198, D-271, D-289. The misspelled synthetic entry deliberately models an error; these fake card names do not claim compatibility with a live catalog. D04 uses a separate complete sample, not the computed count of this short list.

D04 — Resolved import and save choice

Layout: resolved counts and a read-only preview accompany a Deck name field. Save as new / Replace saved deck is an explicit mode choice; replacement identifies the target collection entry. Save deck and Edit pasted list are text actions. Cover selection is optional later metadata, not a forced extra import step.

Interaction: Save as new creates a distinct saved entry; Replace changes the selected saved entry only. Neither changes a lobby/game’s selected copy. Save requires fully resolved definitions and atomic server acceptance; failure retains the previous valid saved deck and editable input. Success returns to D02 (or the calling lobby deck picker when import was launched there). This ordinary form save is not a gameplay Send gate or proof of format legality.

Basis: D-198, D-199, D-221, D-271, D-289. The two-step input/review presentation is proposed and can be simplified during owner review.

D04b — Import review: save controls

Same screen, different scroll position: expose the bottom of D04, including Save deck and Edit pasted list. Long content scrolls; no target shrinks to fit. The selected Save as new example still applies. Choosing Replace instead uses the existing-deck selector on this same form, not an additional Send/upload step. This extra view is a UI-review continuation, not another mandatory route screen.

D05 — Choose a deck cover

Layout: card-name tiles are selectable thumbnails, not card-edit controls. The selected tile has an outline/check plus text. Use selected card confirms the metadata choice; Cancel/Back leaves it unchanged. Landscape uses the short width efficiently while allowing the grid to scroll.

Interaction: select one card already in this deck as its cover. No image upload, crop tool, outside-catalog cover choice or mutation of that card. Text fallback remains available while art is absent. The small selection/confirmation step is a reviewable UI proposal, not a new game-action confirmation requirement. Cover fallback after a later re-import is not decided by these example tiles.

Basis: D-199, D-271.

D06 — Delete a saved deck

Layout: a bounded modal over the collection, with Keep deck and Delete saved deck as text buttons. The destructive button is distinguished by wording as well as styling. Background rows are not interactive while the modal is open.

Interaction: Keep deck/Back cancels this dialog without deleting anything. Delete saved deck requests collection deletion and returns to D01 after success. Selected game/lobby copies survive. No trash folder, gameplay Undo or misleading “Undo deletion” snackbar is offered. A failed deletion reports its actual failure without optimistically claiming permanent success. This one destructive-data confirmation is a proposal, not a universal confirm-every-action policy.

Basis: D-221, D-241; exact confirmation presentation is UI design work.

L01 — Lobby awaiting invitation acceptance

Layout: own deck/preparation, recipient invitation status, starter choice and Ready are distinct. Ready is enabled because this example has an own selected deck, even though riley has not accepted. Cancel game is separate from Back. Random is an illustrative selected value, not an approved universal default.

Interaction: Change deck opens L03; Prepare deck opens L04. Ready can persist before acceptance. The opponent’s later acceptance opens this same lobby without resetting the inviter’s preparation or Ready. Decline retains it and permits Reinvite through the existing-lobby path. Cancel game removes this pending invite and its game; merely leaving the screen does neither. No host Start or expiry.

Basis: D-195, D-201, D-204–D-209, D-287.

L02 — Accepted lobby before own deck selection

Layout: Choose deck is the own-side primary action. Opponent Ready is an explicit status with text/checkmark, not permission to start for them. Own Ready is disabled with the visible reason “Select your deck.” Starter offers either participant or Random; it is not a pre-start reroll.

Interaction: Accepting P01 did not select a deck, Ready or immediately start. Select an existing saved deck through L03; no legality or size check is added. After selection, Prepare deck and enabled Ready use L01/L05’s layout with accepted opponent status. Changes to own deck/preparation/starter clear only the changing player’s Ready. Late lobby edits after the game starts fail normally; the screen must move to the actual active game rather than reopening the lobby.

Basis: D-190, D-191, D-195, D-201, D-204, D-205, D-274.

L03 — Select a game-local deck copy

Layout: saved deck name, cover fallback and descriptive counts accompany each Select text action. Import deck is a secondary escape when the collection lacks the desired deck, not a required detour for normal selection.

Interaction: Select creates/replaces this game’s prepared copy and returns directly to its lobby. It clears own Ready without affecting the opponent’s. It does not edit the saved source, auto-ready or require another Send/confirmation. Deleting/editing the source later leaves this copy intact. Back cancels the picker without changing selection. An empty collection uses the same Import route; there is no automatic blank deck or silent substitute.

Basis: D-189, D-191, D-199, D-205, D-221.

L04 — Prepare mainboard and sideboard

Layout: Mainboard / Library and Sideboard are separate labeled list panels. Selected rows and explicit Move 1 text actions provide discoverable transfer controls without depending on drag precision. Landscape uses equal independently scrollable columns; portrait stacks them. Quantity/name rows summarize copies, not saved-deck editing privileges.

Interaction: choose a row and transfer one copy in either direction; repeat as desired, with no one-for-one or legal-size enforcement. Completed transfers automatically synchronize, clear only own Ready and leave the saved deck alone. No Save preparation/Done-to-send is required. Back simply returns to the lobby. On entering actual play, no Sideboard view/edit/move path exists. The shown per-copy list controls are proposals, not a finalized drag/drop or bulk design.

Basis: D-189, D-191, D-202, D-203, D-259.

L05 — Own Ready accepted

Layout: own Ready is a textual status/checkmark. Withdraw Ready is an explicit action; Change deck/Prepare deck remain discoverable. No host Start button or both-online indicator. Cancel game remains separate and applies only before start.

Interaction: Ready persists after leaving/disconnection; it is not a liveness lease. The second accepted Ready starts once, even while the first player is away. Start shuffles both Libraries, sets life to 20, resolves a selected Random starter and begins turn 1 at Untap, with no automatic opening draw. The extended packet then uses G01 (G00 is the original placeholder). On returning after an accepted game ending, restore last prepared decks, clear both Ready and use this lobby structure in its not-ready state; both must ready again. Back alone never withdraws Ready or cancels the game.

Basis: D-190, D-200, D-204, D-205, D-213, D-274.

L06 — Cancel an unstarted game

Layout: proposed confirmation with Keep game / Cancel game text buttons. The dimmed background is a lobby, not a live game. Back/close keeps the game.

Interaction: either participant can request cancellation before start without the other player’s approval. It removes the current listing and pending invite; there is no trash/restore UI. Leaving the screen is different and preserves the lobby/Ready. If start already won the normal server ordering race, do not cancel or reset that started play; show the current game. Reinvitation must not revive a cancelled lobby. This dialog is not the gameplay result-suggestion/acceptance flow, which is intentionally excluded from the pilot.

Basis: D-205–D-209, D-241, D-287. The extra cancellation confirmation is a reviewable UI proposal, not approval of an extra gameplay-ending confirmation.

G00 — Gameplay intentionally omitted

Layout: only a shell, Back and a clearly labeled empty content area. This gives the non-gameplay navigation a destination and demonstrates two orientations. It does not settle how much space the real board, hand, history or controls get.

Interaction: the original non-gameplay pilot terminated active-game Open and automatic start transitions here; the D-291 extension now uses G01. Start remains automatic on both Ready; there is no Start control here. Back returns to current games, not a shared game Undo, game cancellation or result suggestion. No Sideboard is shown during play.

Scope: this placeholder is retained only for the original pilot’s provenance. The live/history/combat/Stack direction is now pictured below; full card/reveal/ inspection/chat/result overlays and expanded branch navigation remain unpictured.

U01 — Reconnecting and downloaded read-only review

Layout: Reconnecting is a status dialog over the same deliberately empty area. Review downloaded data and Back to games are text navigation actions. This proposes a clear way out of the blocking dialog without enabling mutations.

Interaction: shared actions stay blocked while disconnected, including Undo, Ready, branch activation and new inspection requiring exposure logging. Downloaded read-only navigation remains available. This does not create offline actions or a manual-resend/recovery-center workflow. Same-process reconnect automatically recovers actual already-sent outcomes with original identities. Process restart instead syncs server state and may lose uncommitted local work. Unknown outcome is not rejection; the UI must not invite duplicate submission as a fresh action.

Basis: D-182, D-215, D-216, D-241, D-246, D-252, D-278. The exact dialog escape and wording are UI proposals. This original capture still omits the board; the same blocking/read-only rule applies over the new gameplay layouts.

G01 — Live table and fixed hand

Layout: own battlefield below, opponent above, reflected top/bottom while retaining x positions. Each has an outer darker one-row band and inner lighter two-row band. These are one generic battlefield per player, not new land/ creature zones or type restrictions. All faces point toward the viewer; only ordinary tapped cards rotate. Empty slots/rows are visual framing, not a capacity limit. The camera can pan beyond occupied columns by a still-unspecified margin.

Fixed versus movable: the owner’s Hand hovers below the land band and above bottom controls, independent of board panning. The proposed opponent Hand is a covered top row. Both players’ Library/Graveyard/Exile counts and proposed life grouping occupy the central strip in portrait, a left sidebar in landscape. The board camera alone pans/zooms; fixed docks do not become shared placement. Small abstract thumbnails stand in for zoomable cards, not legible full-size faces. Dense states may need vertical navigation; readable minimum card/peek targets and expanded Hand geometry still need device/gesture review.

Controls: bottom-left tap Undo / hold Redo; bottom-center contextual actions; bottom-right current mode. The proposed mode square opens explicit Normal / Select / Ping choices. Select toggles membership editing without clearing the selection when turned off; Ping consumes its taps. Phase tap opens the existing tracking picker, not an automatic game action. History opens personal review. Overflow exposes Redo, Chat and full Game actions; a generic Actions affordance does not invent a phase shortcut or remove the full per-card action paths.

Gestures: normal single tap opens captured-scope card Actions; double tap performs one selection-aware tap/untap. Hold inspects; drag moves the captured card/selection. Empty-space drag selects; two-finger pan/pinch navigates. These are documented interactions, not functioning gestures in these static files. Own/opponent hidden-face rules remain unchanged. No in-game Sideboard, Send, presence, turn lock or inferred card rules.

Basis: D-267/D-281, D-259 and D-291; board/inspection contracts. Life placement, top Hand and control shapes remain review proposals.

G02 — Live combat and populated Stack

Layout: Stack and combat occupy distinct central lanes between battlefields. Combat uses blockers above attackers in visible pairs; dashed occurrences denote projections whose real sources remain in their green battlefield positions. Stack distinguishes an actual card from an independent effect projection. They are not ordinary three-card visual piles and do not share that capacity limit.

Actions: during Declare attackers with a selection, offer Declare + tap / Without tap. The first composes occurrence entry and individual source taps; the second preserves source orientation. The center quick-action strip can scroll horizontally without moving Undo/mode controls. Full constituent paths remain available outside the quick window. Neither rendering this state nor entering a phase declares attackers, closes combat, resolves Stack or calculates damage.

Combat persists until explicit closure, including when empty. Ordinary phase advancement does not close it. Moving a source out of Battlefield cleans up its combat occurrences, not its independent Stack effects. Card-directed edits through live projections affect the real source; occurrence removal is separate. Dense combat may need board navigation rather than smaller fixed controls. Empty/open, many-pair and frozen-token-effect visuals remain further review states.

Basis: D-112–D-158, D-176, D-242/D-253 and D-291.

H01 — Historical review paused at an exact event

Layout: the table/Hand show the selected historical boundary. Live editing chrome is replaced with Previous / Play / Next at the bottom, and the path timeline immediately above. The exact X marker can lie inside a playback group. Diagonal branch stubs indicate retained alternatives, not a full expanded tree. Off-path navigation needs a further branch-selection view; a stub is not itself permission to activate, archive or delete anything.

Interaction: Previous/Next navigate groups; timeline drag selects individual mutation boundaries and updates the board during the drag. Board animation uses the displayed-to-selected endpoint, not a compulsory queue of every passed node. Phase is read-only; gameplay edits, Undo/Redo, quick actions and mode input are hidden. Permitted local inspection/navigation remains, but a hidden-information request is not silently issued by browsing. Sync continues while paused, with normal deleted-cursor ancestor fallback.

Continue playing from here is distinct from Play. It arms intent at the exact selected event and exposes gameplay controls (H03), without creating a fork. Back to live uses the existing catch-up/changed-path traversal toward the shared continuation, not an unexplained snapshot jump; viewing a branch does not activate it. Offline review never enables this gameplay continuation route.

Basis: D-177/D-179, D-238/D-245, D-277 and D-291.

H02 — Grouped playback running

Interaction: Pause stops personal playback, not server sync. Touching/dragging the timeline pauses first, then scrubs exact events. Continue playing from here also pauses at the selected concrete boundary and arms intent; it is not the transport Play action. Each playback group animates its net start-to-end board change; separate groups remain staged even if downloaded together.

Returning: backgrounded games with unpresented updates enter this playback flow from the last presented/reviewed context. Changed paths retain the specified common-ancestor rollback before catch-up. Reaching the shared live boundary returns to live; an expected own confirmation alone does not manufacture a replay. No autoplay preference, speed default, finished-game archive or animation timing is chosen by this mockup.

Basis: D-177/D-277 and D-291. Historical no-edit chrome matches H01.

H03 — Historical continuation armed before first action

State: “Continuing from A · no action yet” distinguishes the displayed past from ordinary live following. This is an armed personal intent, not a third authoritative game state. The old future remains retained and active until a successful explicit continuation mutation creates/activates the new line. Cancel / Return to live before that action only leaves personal intent; there is no empty branch to delete. Failure/no-change likewise does not create one.

Undo clarification: old A → B → C, new A → X → Y: eligible latest-own Undo may remove Y and then X, including the first action immediately after the fork. It leaves the current boundary at A without automatically returning to B→C. The fork point A cannot be undone/crossed while it actually has multiple retained child continuations. Recompute eligibility after each accepted Undo: removing the last action of a new line does not leave a permanent “was once a fork” lock, but the remaining linear future still participates in ordinary replay checks. Author, revealing-action, dependency, replay-work and later-fork checks still apply. This addresses accidental branch creation using the existing rule; it is not unconditional cancellation of any action or recall of a sent request.

Undo availability/target remains based on shared current history, not the personal historical cursor. When a server accepts a locally withdrawn request later, its accepted effect still arrives normally. Exact banner wording and return/Cancel placement are proposals; the intent and server boundary are not.

Basis: D-179, D-224/D-233/D-245, D-258/D-277 and D-291.

G03 — Explicit Redo and mode chooser routes

Redo arbitration: tap Undo invokes Undo only; recognizing a hold invokes Redo only. No Undo on press-down, no Undo on release after a hold and no automatic repeat is selected here. The controls menu exposes labeled Redo and native accessibility must provide an equivalent explicit action, without requiring a timed hold. Both routes use the same server-authoritative per-player game stack, eligibility and retry rules. Exact hold interval/feedback is still UI work.

Menus: overflow is a proposed route to Chat and Game actions, not a newly invented settings suite. Game actions must retain existing tracking, random, token, combat and ending paths; this packet does not yet picture their complete menus or editors. The separate bottom-right mode square opens Normal / Select / Ping, rather than silently cycling modes. It does not open this overflow menu. Choice-sheet layout remains unpictured; normal/Select/Ping tap semantics are already specified. Close/Back dismisses without a shared edit.

Basis: D-235/D-259, D-267/D-281 and D-291. No claim that an incidental enabled/disabled color proves the complete eligibility computation.

Whole-journey interaction budgets

These are draft counts for the proposed route, not measured Android tests. A “tap” means one explicit activation; typing/pasting, scrolling and keyboard dismissal are additional interaction cost, not hidden zero-cost steps.

Starting state → goal Proposed route and explicit activations Additional work
Main menu → existing active game Games → Open: 2 taps, or a visible landscape navigation game row: 1 tap. Portrait drawer → game: 2 taps; list scrolling if needed.
Main menu → accept a visible invite Games → Accept: 2 taps, arriving in the same lobby, not Ready. Invitations follows Games; scrolling if needed.
Main menu → invite a saved contact Contacts → Invite: 2 taps, arriving in waiting lobby. Contact-list scrolling if needed.
Main menu → search, add and invite Contacts → Search field → Search → Add contact → Invite: 5 taps. Type username; keyboard/scroll cost may add taps.
Main menu → save a new imported list Manage decks → Import → list field → Review import → name field → Save deck: 6 taps. Paste/type list and name; correction/keyboard/scroll cost.
Accepted lobby without a deck → Ready Choose deck → Select → Ready: 3 taps. Deck-list scrolling if needed. No legality/size confirmation.
Preparation open → transfer one copy Select row → Move 1: 2 taps. List scrolling if needed; repeated moves must not add a Send step.
Ready lobby → leave without withdrawing Back: 1 tap. No cancellation or publication prompt.
Saved-deck details → delete collection entry Delete saved deck → confirm deletion: 2 taps. Copies selected in games survive.
Live → exact history → armed continuation History → drag timeline → Continue playing from here: 2 taps + 1 drag. If playback is running, dragging itself pauses before scrubbing; no separate Pause tap. First gameplay mutation is additional and alone creates/activates continuation.
Live → eligible Redo Hold Undo: 1 hold, or overflow → Redo: 2 taps. No earlier Undo emitted; hold timing/native accessibility still need validation.

The import review split, cover confirmation and cancellation dialog are intentional pilot proposals whose interaction cost should be reviewed, not silently declared optimal. Reaching a visible button may require scrolling in short landscape or with a keyboard; the later large-text/keyboard review must count that cost too.

Coverage and limits

Pictured: 28 primary screen/state drafts (27 Stitch-derived plus locally composed N02) and two scrolled continuations, all in both orientations: 60 captures. These include the shared navigation, inline sign-in error, submitted reset request, unresolved import, two import save modes in one state, collection-deletion modal, waiting invitation, no-own-deck lobby, preparation, accepted Ready, cancellation modal and reconnect dialog, plus six gameplay states: live, populated Stack/combat, paused exact history, running playback, armed continuation and explicit Redo menu.

Described but not separately pictured: clean authentication forms, network and field errors, invalid reset link, empty/loading/search-no-results lists, rename editor, import lookup-in-progress/save failure, replacing-mode selection, returned-lobby not-ready state and successful reconnect. These still need visual state completion before claiming that every non-gameplay state is designed. Gameplay expansions still needed include Hand expansion, phase/mode choice sheets, card/zone action menus, readable inspector, shared View/Reveal trays, dense/empty combat variants, branch selection/return/archive views, chat/comments and ending dialogs, plus selected/conflict/reconnect/large-text/gesture variants over the real board. Static examples do not settle all camera bounds, hit regions or timings.

Not claimed: final visual style, full keyboard/large-text/tablet/foldable coverage, touch/accessibility usability validation, live Android behavior, exhaustive state/concurrency testing or a passed UI/review gate. Platform notification permission dialogs/settings belong to Android; this revision removes their old main-menu shortcut, not OS authority or notification behavior. No custom mute/settings screen or replacement shortcut is invented.

Behavior and UI discrepancies found during review are documentation/design work, not permission to add features or start application implementation.

Provenance and review artifacts

The layouts were requested from Google Stitch in the private design project 6617750535460836476 on 2026-10-21. Static HTML exports, generation briefs and the screen manifest are retained with this packet. Each responsive source is captured at both fixed viewports; no portrait screenshot is stretched to make a landscape image. Review captures, not Stitch’s default large canvas preview, are the images embedded here.

D-292 owner revision: all sources/captures now apply the cumulative feedback: fullscreen, current branding, same-card sign-in, reset-copy removal, shared Menu/Games navigation and combined games-before-invites browser. N02 is an additional locally composed state; these revisions were made to local inert derivatives, not claimed as new cloud edits. Historical generation briefs/raw sources are retained unchanged as provenance, not current instructions.

See generation briefs and source manifest. The exported HTML is design material with executable interactions removed, not production frontend/application scaffolding. Any documented normalization or repair of generated presentation is recorded in the manifest/build notes rather than silently attributed to Stitch.

Gameplay source distinction: six new designs exist in the same Stitch project. Their raw .stitch.html.txt outputs are retained, but the packet captures substantially locally recomposed inert derivatives, not pixel-identical cloud exports. The derivatives harmonize G01’s gray/teal abstract-card vocabulary across all six states, fit both battlefield halves into the sparse initial framing, restore clipped history controls, separate fixed docks from the board camera and remove invented Pass/concession/Declare Action wording. H01/H02 use a sparse closed-combat historical boundary; G02 illustrates populated combat separately. The repaired reference HTML/CSS was then sent back to Stitch’s edit operation, creating six corrected editable cloud revisions in the same project. Initial and revised raw outputs and their resource IDs are retained in the manifest; a cloud revision does not prove pixel identity with the local derivative. Use this packet for the checked portrait/landscape comparison, and Stitch for the editable originals/revisions; neither is an approved implementation or final geometry.

Review repairs included removing Stitch-invented 60/15-card size restrictions from lobby/preparation wording, describing definition resolution rather than catalog authenticity, restoring a clipped landscape Back target and widening a landscape reset form that had accidentally retained its portrait width limit. The minimum-target normalization also makes some short landscape panels scroll; it must not be mistaken for a completed native accessibility review.

The UI draft index explains rebuild and private hosting. HTML and PDF are compiled from this same Markdown and use the same embedded image files. Review progress is not a separate source of game behavior.
